title: `teploy sandbox new|stop|resume|fork --json` (rev 23, sandbox-v1): one sandbox as the engine on the server reports it. Failures use the error envelope on stderr and never emit this shape.

server.description: The server as the command was given it (--host).

host.description: The SSH host the server resolved to.

id.description: A 26-character ULID: the sandbox's identity for its whole life (stop and resume keep it).

image.description: What the sandbox was created from.

network.description: none, allowlist or open. A value not listed here is passed through as the engine reported it.

user.description: The account commands run as in the sandbox: root, or the engine's sandbox user.

state.description: running or stopped. A consumer must treat any other value as not finished, and ask again.

expires_at.description: The running deadline. A stopped run ignores it (retain_until governs it instead).

on_expire.description: destroy or stop: what the engine does with the sandbox at expires_at.

labels.description: The run's labels. The CLI adds one of its own to every sandbox it makes (teploy.cli-run), which is how a create whose answer was lost is found again.

retain_until.description: Only while stopped: when the engine deletes the sandbox and its filesystem.

forked_from.description: Only on a fork: the sandbox it was started from.

usage.description: What the engine has measured. A measure the engine did not take is absent, never zero: a consumer must not read its absence as 0.

running_sec.description: Seconds spent running, summed across stop and resume.

disk_bytes.description: The latest observed size of what the sandbox has written: a level, not a running total.
